item.title: Re: Real Life Publishing Opportunities
item.content:encoded:
OUT THERE: Into the Queer New Yonder is looking for YA queer futuristic science fiction.

The story requirements are simple:

4-8 thousand words
YA fiction set in the future (any genre)
Queer author, queer protagonist
The story you wish you had when you were 16
Does not have to be #ownvoices
Does not have to contain romantic elements

What you get if selected:

Publication in OUT THERE: Into the Queer New Yonder anthology, edited by Saundra Mitchell; published by Inkyard Press.
$900 (US) plus a pro-rated share of any royalties received on the sale of the anthology.
We ask for exclusive rights from acceptance to 2 years from publication date. Exceptions will be made for Best Of/Year Of/Awards anthologies.
All rights revert 2 years from publication date of OUT THERE anthology. (On resale, we’d appreciate a credit, “First appeared in OUT THERE, 2022.”)
We ask for publication and audio rights for that term. All other rights remain with you.
You must be at least 13 years old to submit to this anthology. Authors 13-18 years old must co-sign their contract with their parent/guardian if selected for publication.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] Big Red Button
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout w/ ACS, lots of addenda to expand on the concept, short testing logs and an incident report.

Elevator Pitch: It has the appearance of an ATM machine, with a glass front screen and 2 buttons on the ATM's base where the keypad normally is; the left button is red, and the right button is blue. The card reader slot on a normal ATM machine is used to insert a piece of paper/papyrus, and then a button can be pressed. Red will paint an image where someone close to the person who activated it is depicted doing something (anything can be pictured), and the Foundation does not want anybody to know what the blue button does, since it does something so veil-breaking.

Central Narrative: The story will be carried through an incident report, an interview log, testing logs, and addenda. The addenda will show how much the Foundation tried to keep the item secret, and prohibit any activation of the blue button. They started to implement procedures to try and keep it from being abused, and then after they did that, they opened it up again, but they still need to keep the blue button as a last resort.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story will be carried in-depth, and the mystery of what the second button will do and why it's so important to keep it even though it will be veil-breaking.

Additional Notes: This idea has been in my head for a while, and I just wanted to get it out there.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I think you can make that work, but you should work on the narrative. Just explaining some properties and adding a log about how it got found won't make the cut, so I'd change the structure:
- leave out most details from the actual description and focus on a log about the discovery.
- try to focus on external input for the log(s) (e.g. in a found footage style), because if the foundation writes the logs, you have to do it in a clinical way, which would take away much tension. Maybe use interview logs or diary entries by the victim or whatever, this way you can build up narrative tension more deliberately, finishing with the conclusion about his room mate.

Anyway, that are just my 5 cent, I'm not experienced in crits, so take it with a small grain of salt.

item.title: Re: Be Careful What You Wish For
item.content:encoded:
(Can't give Greenlights)

This is a somewhat simple concept. I'm unsure whether it bears any resemblance to articles already on the site, but the idea of a laptop that can tell you when you're going to die feels a bit generic. That being said, the concept of exploring the existential and universal fear of death is something that definitely deserves to be developed and written.

+ Here's some crit
- Begone crit

SCP is a laptop that contains images of how it's user will die.

I don't see why this has to be some kind of everyday item. A strange artifact, technology, creature, plant, or anything that could simply convey images into the mind of an individual could be used instead. The physical design of an SCP is an important aspect for standing out in your reader's minds. There's limitless ways to be imaginative in this department, so don't be afraid to get creative!

Too many subversions of the images will cause the user to enter a comatose state from which they cannot recover, and they cannot die. They are fully conscious in the coma, being able to see, hear, smell, feel, etc.

Why exactly? Wouldn't it eventually just end up showing them dying in a hospital bed if they avoided all other premature deaths?

It's an interesting idea, but it robs your narrative of a lot of its punch. Instead of having the researcher in your story simply fall into a coma, perhaps have him realize that death is truly inescapable. Or perhaps (this is a little generic I'll admit) have it so that the universe is trying to correct the imbalance caused by his avoidance of death. The research is then driven insane, either by the knowledge that death is unavoidable, or by the increasingly absurd ways in which the universe is trying to kill him. Maybe both.

Main narrative will follow a Junior Researcher fearing the death they see for themself. They become obsessed with avoiding death using the laptop and eventually go too far and have to face the consequences of never dying, but not really living.

Hinting at the fate of the Researcher in the description and containment procedures, and seeing how the relatable fear of death can push someone to act in a way that they know is wrong.

I really enjoy this narrative, even if it is a little generic or perhaps played out. My suggestion would be to really focus on conveying the existential fear of death through wording in the various logs made by the researcher. If you end up getting greenlighted, I'd suggest contacting reviewers who specialize in this kind of writing when you post your draft.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Be Careful What You Wish For

Solid concept, good execution, but the numbers are too off, that break it to me.

A velocity of 10 m/s is just 36 Km/h (less than 22.5 miles/hour), terminal velocity for a pine cone isn't much more than throwing them by hand, and the force of the explosion wasn't given. So, as far as I'm aware, this isn't nearly as dangerous as it is purported to be.

It isn't Keter, either. Even if you make it more dangerous than a modern ICBM its containment is quite reliable, and I see no reason to be otherwise. This is a solid Euclid.

You don't need to make this more dangerous. You can correct the numbers to really make it into a war-worthy missile, or you can go with the numbers and make it a freak flying tree with annoying dropping cones and a somewhat dangerous blast at the end. It works either way, if not better with the current low numbers.

item.title: Re: Book of the undead
item.content:encoded:
The idea of the SCP reminds me a little of King's Pet Sematary.

Since the SCP is very simple, I think you should focus on its narrative.

I mean, if dead people is revived as monsters at the second time, a cult could be doing an army of monsters. Or a new religion could be using that to make miracles reviving people and gaining more followers. With more believers the creatures the book make are more powerful, and the Foundation needs to contain it before something very powerful is born, etc.

And why the book revives people? Why the second time they are born as anomalous creatures? Theres a lot of storytelling you could work there!

Have a great day!

:D

item.title: Be Careful What You Wish For
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Genre (Optional): Tragedy

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article with tests logs, emails, and security footage.

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a laptop that contains images of how it's user will die. It's possible to avoid the death that the images show, but they will be replaced with the new eventual death of the user.(Example: A morbidly obese man may see images of himself dying of heart failure in a hospital. Exercising and losing weight would change his fate, and the images would show his death coming much later.) Too many subversions of the images will cause the user to enter a comatose state from which they cannot recover, and they cannot die. They are fully conscious in the coma, being able to see, hear, smell, feel, etc.

Central Narrative: Main narrative will follow a Junior Researcher fearing the death they see for themself. They become obsessed with avoiding death using the laptop and eventually go too far and have to face the consequences of never dying, but not really living. Test logs and emails will show their growing obsession with using the SCP to avoid death, and surveillance log will show how that obsession culminates in unauthorized access to the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Hinting at the fate of the Researcher in the description and containment procedures, and seeing how the relatable fear of death can push someone to act in a way that they know is wrong.

Additional Notes: I've struggled in the past with having a "story" in my ideas so I'm particularly interested if I'm more on track this time.

I think this is a novel idea, but the problem for me is there doesn't really seem to be any pull.

Yes, it's original, but it feels like there's almost nothing going on, and there's nothing to attract. I understand that it is a new idea, and nothing has been done regarding the bee movie I don't think, but that doesn't really seem like it justifies a whole SCP.

Is there anything else to it other than the bee movie not actually existing?), I would be inclined to like it more, but as it stands it doesn't seem all that special to me.

item.title: Collapsable side panel on all browser sizes
item.content:encoded:
Description: Wikidot uses adaptive scaling for its UI elements. There is a navigation panel on the left side of the site that, when the screen is less than 768 pixels1, collapses off screen with a button to bring it in and out. I request that this panel have be collapsible regardless of window size (although it would be open by default for medium-large screens). An example of this behavior can be found here.

If this is not possible, a simpler option would be to change the 768 breakpoint to a larger value. For this I conjecture that 1500 pixels would be approximately correct.

Reason: The side panel does not adapt well to tablet devices. When using a tablet device in portrait mode, the panel is stuck taking up about a third of the screen, while providing little value. This, in my opinion, dramatically harms the reading experience. This problem is easily remedied for all devices by making the panel collapsible.

In the event that this is not feasible, I suggest a breakpoint of 1500 pixels based on my knowledge of common device sizes. Once you step down from a desktop monitor, devices are almost exclusively tablets and smartphones2. On either of those devices, the panel should be hidden by default, regardless of their horizontal resolution. For this reason, I suggest a value that is only a little lower than the standard horizontal resolution on a modern device, while still allowing for some padding for DPI scaled devices, such as laptops. This solution has weird edge cases, and could easily cause problems for other device sizes, so I don't recommend it unless there is no better option.

Advantages:

  • Improved readability for tablet devices, and other large portrait screens (some desktop setups use a "sideways" monitor for reading).
  • More economical use of screen space

Disadvantages:

  • Slight increase in UI "clutter", as a new button would need to be added
  • Increases required clicks by 1 for some navigation tasks on some browsers
Footnotes
1. This is the breakpoint listed in the CSS. In practice, the value will change based on various scaling settings of the device, because nothing is ever simple.
2. When considering actual hardware resolution. Laptops considerably complicate this problem because they frequently use DPI scaling, making them appear lower resolution than they actually are. My 1080p laptop "looks" like it has a horizontal resolution of 1650 pixels, because of DPI scaling.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) the Survivors
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Never thought that the GOC could declare war on 85% of the Milky Way Galaxy, but man were we wrong.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
- hide block

SCP-XXXX is an alien cargo ship that was shot down by the GOC, even though the GOC considered this as a victory sense it was the first ship that project space cannon took down, both SCP-XXXX/1 and the Foundation think otherwise.

The reason why is because the GOC just declare war to the Capital Planet, an advanced civilization that controls 85% of the Trinity galaxy.

SCP-XXXX/1 have an appearance of a human with most of their body being black and their chin, throat, chest and belly white, instead of an anus they have black tails with a white underside and a large fluke at the end, they also have large white patches above each eye and a dorsal fin which starts at the back of the hand to in between the shoulder blades.

SCP-XXXX/1 stands about 6 feet high on average and weights 250 pounds on average, SCP-XXXX/1 are incredibly strong, fast, intelligent and speaks english.

they were discovered by the foundation on a beach in Honolulu, Hawaii where they were exiting their escape pods, people on the beach began to call the police until the Hawaiian branch of the foundation came in with large bus’s and class A amnestics, over a thousand of them were transported.

SCP-XXXX was carrying over a hundred monoliths also known as SCP-XXXX/2, the monoliths were made of an unknown element never seen before, but the monoliths are considered safe, the gravitonium contained in these monoliths are actually more deadly, the gravitonium also known as SCP-XXXX/3 appears to be a liquid metal that is constantly moving, SCP-XXXX/3 also have the ability to manipulate gravity depending on the temperature, if hot it pull everything into it and if cool then it will repeal everything.

When SCP-XXXX crashed 20 miles west of San Francisco most of the monoliths were destroyed and the gravitonium escaped into the air, not only that but some of the monoliths were sucked out of the ship while it was in space and these things are now landing in area’s where more of SCP-XXXX/3 is hidden underground, these areas include Utah, California and Romania.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: there’s 2 Hooks with this SCP idea.
The first being SCP-XXXX/3 the gravitonium, if the Foundation managed to create an SCP-XXXX/2 the monoliths then they would be able to use SCP-XXXX/3 for artificial gravity and travel faster than the speed of light, this SCP could change the Foundation in the near future if successfully contained and controlled.
The second being the Capital Planet which have a strong government, a strong military and controls 85% of the entire galaxy, The Capital Planet could be a new Group of Interest sense they share some of the same goals, to protect humanity even though the Capital actually protects all underdeveloped civilizations, and the Foundation pacifically one of the O5 counsel could gain a seat in the galactic senate allowing the foundation to have an influence on the galaxy.

Additional Notes: this SCP idea is spit up in 2 forms, 1 being about the SCP itself and 1 about Project Space Cannon and why the GOC built it, there is also going to be a series of events that took place in the ship before its doom.

item.title: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Action
Page Layout: Might include a journal written by the SCP later in the article's progression
Elevator Pitch: The SCP entity has the ability to passively possess any sentient beings within a certain radius upon the termination of the previous host. Upon possession, it will immediately overwrite the host's brain with the entity's personality. SCP-1 will also have an increase in intelligence/IQ scaling according to the intelligence of the host pre-possession (the smarter the host, the smarter SCP-1 is). SCP-1 is initially oblivious to the fact that they possesses people.
SCP-1 has an affinity to create advanced weapons. The dangerousness of the weapons also scale with the intelligence of the host. Due to this, the Foundation facilitates the containment of the entity by guaranteeing the termination of it’s previous host within suitable range of a “dumb” enough host. Foundation researchers theorize that given a smart enough host, SCP-1 could cause a XK-Class Scenario.
Central Narrative: The SCP is actually a character from a fictional universe in the SCP universe, who somehow got into the base SCP universe through a reality anomaly. The entity has a confused memory of its life, and is missing many details about itself.
Someone working the Foundation comments on the similarities they saw between SCP-1 and a character in a show that they watched as a kid to SCP-1, the entity is confused by the character's name, aggressively claiming to not be/know the character. The SCP slowly regains a sense of self awareness throughout the article due to this, slowly regaining memories and gradually realizing what it is, going insane.
The Foundation also is looking into utilizing its intelligence increase potential on Foundation employees to help create anomalous weapons that would help the containment of other SCPs.
Hook: The premise of a SCP slowly losing its mind due to it being foreign to the universe and its rules.
Additional Notes: The SCP’s original universe’s narrative is subject to change as I want to make its backstory integral to the narrative. I also want to add an experiment log with some of the creations SCP-1 has created during testing.
Would love to see any form of critique, but especially on how original the idea is and how interesting the idea is.
This is my first time doing an idea, so I appreciate everyone reading through it!

item.title: The town of blackberry
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Thriller

Page Layout (Optional): My plan is to split the first and last accounts, first being a relay of a video feed, the second being an interview

Elevator Pitch: A tribe surrounded by mutant blackberry vines and the tribe's unique traditions

Central Narrative: MTF team "Tillermen" investigate a dome of mutant blackberry vines. The vines are huge and grow back fast. The team finds a tribe that lives in the ruins a former small town. The tribe is a bit deformed having little access to sunlight, but still seems to be in good health. They explain to the team their traditions that keeps them safe from the blackberry vines. what stands out the most is how the vines are more aggressive towards non-organic material, and a ritual where the tribe sends transgressors into a dense growth just outside the village as a form of spirit walk. The team tries to enter with their gear, but cant due to the density of the growth.

+ show block
– hide block

They agree to go along with traditions and walk in naked. Only two return, both panicked. One decides to remain with the village and the other returns to base. He is interviewed and explains what he saw inside the dense. There were waves of vines that would move across the floor, and vine covered creatures would walk through walls, both seen to swallow rocks and small bits of metal. There was one massive open room which housed a colossal blackberry with thousands of little black spheres. The team member claims he saw his own reflection, but he looked different somehow. When he looked away, he saw two team members sprouting vines from their head. The remaining three ran away perused by the vine monsters. One more team member died after falling through the floor, but the two escape after a close call. The story closes with the MTF's belief as to where the mutant blackberries came from.


Additional Notes: I didn't bother to develop the characters in this draft since its not super critical to the central narrative. It saves me some space since I still have to meet the word count.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Standard SCP pages and test logs

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid dressed in casual street attire, who asks people within a ten foot radius of itself if they would like to make a donation. Anything is a valid donation, and upon receiving the donation, will proceed to put it out of sight before asking whom/what the contributor wishes to be the receiver of the donation. Refusal to donate or acknowledge the entity will result in increasingly aggressive behavior.

Central Narrative: (Attempted) interviews and test logs will be used to tell the story of the article

Hook: I feel like the specifics and the potential of the SCP's abilities are interesting, and there is probably going to be some added gore and spook material added in there as well.

item.title: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

I find the image of a trans person physically slicing the embodiment of transphobia from themselves to be very powerful, and the final line is basically the closest this thing can have to a happy ending. I'm wondering, do you have any suggestions for making that final paragraph more impactful or obviously important to the metaphor?

The problem here is that making it land better feels like it's…a lot more likely to feel jarring? Really though, my issue is more that the ending feels…not climactic enough? And I'm not sure how to make this feel more climactic tbh without leaning more into the darkness. This said: it might just be my natural inclination towards darker writing that's coming through here rather than an objective truth.

I did consider this, but decided against it as really, these aren't parasites as we understand them but are rather the embodiment of the gender that people feel a trans person should have. Therefore, their ultimate purpose is to totally usurp the host like a cuckoo bird, not to propagate.

Like, I get this and accept your reasoning for this but it feels, to me, a little too loose and up in the air without the propagation; but at the end of the day, this is your call.

I'm not sure how to incorporate it or trim it, although it seems important for thematic purposes that it remain in some form.

It'd work better if there was some additional connection here; where like, -1 is the only one who can affect which way -2 goes but it feels…too much like that'd be putting everything on one person when really it's everyone that affects stuff. Honestly, I don't think it really adds much and I'd just trim it completely if you're not going to e.g. tie it into the end cycle or something instead.

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX
item.content:encoded:
Well basically, by investigating that room and the house that it is in, they discover that years ago, 7 young girls who had a slumber party there were found dead in the room. The police never found out what happened, but the Foundation suspect another potential SCP to have been responsible. When they died, the room was impregnated with the remnants of the girls' souls with the feeling they had when they died. That's how SCP-XXXX was created. Now, whenever someone enters the room, they are "possessed" by the remnants, and act as previously described. The remnents then behave like some kind of virus, spreading from one person to another through a pillow fight. That's why it could potentially cause the end of the world. If everyone starts running around giggling and pillowfighting forever, human civilization would collapse.

As to how to bring it up, I was thinking of having the Foundation investigate and learn about the 7 girls (as previously stated), then do experiences and talking with one of the possessed one. Then they'll understand that this person is possessed with the remnants of the girls' souls though dialogue.

I know it sounds jarring, but that's why I like it. I love SCPs that are seemingly funny or ridiculous, just to be revealed to actually be dangerous and creepy.
